titleEn: X Spaces: Conversation with Donald Trump
titleZh: X Spaces：与唐纳德·特朗普的对话
summaryEn: Musk hosted Donald Trump for a roughly two-hour X Spaces conversation on the 2024 campaign, the economy, immigration and censorship; the start was delayed about 40 minutes by technical problems Musk attributed to a cyberattack.
summaryZh: 马斯克主持了一场与唐纳德·特朗普进行的、时长约2小时的 X Spaces 对话，讨论了2024年竞选、经济、移民和审查制度；由于技术问题，对话开始时间推迟了约40分钟，马斯克将其归因于一次网络攻击。

segments.textEn: All right. Hello, everyone. So my apologies for the late start. We unfortunately had a massive distributed denial of service attack against our servers and saturated all of our data lines. Like, basically hundreds of gigabits of data were saturated.
segments.textZh: 好了。大家好。很抱歉这么晚才开始。遗憾的是，我们的服务器遭到了一次大规模分布式拒绝服务攻击，所有数据线路都达到了饱和状态。就像，基本上数百吉比特的数据都达到了饱和状态。

segments.textEn: We think we've overcome most of that, and so it's not time to proceed. But as this massive attack illustrates, there's a lot of opposition to people just hearing what President Trump has to say. And so. But I'm honored to have this conversation. I want to emphasize it's a conversation and it's really intended to just get a feel for what Donald Trump is. Just like in a conversation, it's hard to catch a vibe about someone if you just don't hear them talk in a normal way.
segments.textZh: 我们认为，我们已经克服了其中的大部分问题，所以现在还不是继续的时候。但正如这次大规模攻击所表明的那样，有很多人反对让人们仅仅听听特朗普总统要说什么。所以。可是，我很荣幸能进行这次对话。我想强调，这是一场对话，它真正的目的只是让大家感受一下唐纳德·特朗普是什么样的人。就像在对话中一样，如果你就是听不到某人以正常的方式讲话，就很难感受到这个人给人的感觉。

segments.textEn: And when, you know, when there's an adversarial interview, like no one's themselves in an adversarial interview.
segments.textZh: 而当，你知道，当进行一场对抗性采访时，就像没有人在对抗性采访中会是他们自己。

And I hope we can have something like that today. We.
segments.textZh: 所以你可以了解，比如，什么，什么是，你知道，进行一场对话究竟是什么样的？所以很荣幸，唐纳德。很高兴，真的很高兴能，能交谈。正如你昨天提到的，我们昨天进行了一场很棒的对话。如果我们当时能直接把那场对话录下来并发布出去，那就太棒了。我希望我们今天也能有类似的对话。我们。

We view that as an honor. And then you do want silencing of certain voices. Usually those are voices that have something to say that are constructive, oftentimes constructive. And so we have to consider it an honor. But congratulations on breaking every record in the book tonight.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我想我们会的。我很确定我们会的。也祝贺你，因为我看到你以数百万人参与打破了所有纪录。这是一种荣幸。我们视之为一种荣幸。而且，你确实想让某些声音噤声。通常，那些声音是有话要说、具有建设性的声音，往往具有建设性。所以我们必须将其视为一种荣幸。不过，祝贺你今晚打破了所有纪录。

segments.textEn: That's great.
segments.textZh: 那太好了。

segments.textEn: Well, thank you. Well, maybe we could start off with, I mean, the assassination attempt, which was an incredible thing. And I have to say that your actions after that assassination attempt were inspiring.
segments.textZh: 嗯，谢谢。嗯，也许我们可以从，我是说，那次暗杀未遂开始，那是一件令人难以置信的事。而且我必须说，你在那次暗杀未遂后的举动鼓舞了人心。

segments.textEn: Instead of shying away from things, instead of ducking down, you were popping your fist in there and saying, fight, fight, fight. And I think that's, I mean, you know, the President of the United States represents America. And I think that is, that is America. That, that is strength under fire. And so that's, you know, a big, you know, part of the reason why I was excited to endorse you as the, the President, United States, for having the term here is that was, that was just incredibly inspiring.
segments.textZh: 你没有躲避，没有俯身缩下去，而是在那里挥舞拳头，说，战斗，战斗，战斗。我认为那就是，我是说，你知道，美国总统代表美国。而我认为那就是，那就是美国。那，那就是炮火之下的坚强。所以那就是，你知道，我很兴奋支持你成为，成为总统，美国，任期在这里的一个重要，你知道，原因，因为那实在是，那实在是令人难以置信地鼓舞人心。

segments.textEn: But, but, I mean, what was it like for you?
segments.textZh: 但是，但是，我的意思是，对你来说那是什么感觉？

segments.textEn: Not pleasant.
segments.textZh: 并不愉快。

segments.textZh: 我说那是血。

segments.textEn: I had more blood.
segments.textZh: 我有更多的血。

segments.textEn: I didn't know I didn't know I had that much blood. The doctors later told me that the ear is a place that is a very bloody place if you're going to get hit. But in this case, it was probably the best alternative you could even think about because it went at the right angle. And, you know, it was a hard hit. It was very, I guess you would say, surreal, but it wasn't surreal. You know, I was telling somebody, you have instances like this or like a lot less than this, where you feel it's a surreal situation.
segments.textZh: 我不知道，我不知道我有那么多血。医生后来告诉我，如果你要被击中，耳朵是一个非常容易流血的地方。但在这种情况下，它可能是你所能想到的最佳替代结果，因为它以正确的角度击中了。还有，你知道，那一下很重。那非常，我想你会说，超现实，但又不是超现实。你知道，我当时跟某个人说，你会遇到像这样的情况，或者远不及这样的情况，而你会觉得那是一种超现实的情形。

segments.textEn: And I never felt that way. I knew immediately that it was a bullet. I knew immediately that it was at the ear.
segments.textZh: 而我从来没有那种感觉。我立刻就知道那是一颗子弹。我立刻就知道它打在了耳朵上。

segments.textEn: Yeah.
segments.textZh: 对。

segments.textEn: And because it, you know, it hit very hard, but hit the ear. And I also heard people shout, bullets, bullets. You know, get down, get down. Because I, you know, I moved down pretty nicely pretty quickly, and we had bullets flying right over my head after I went down. So I'm glad I went down. The bigger miracle was that I was looking in the exact direction of the shooter. And so it hit. It hit me at an angle that was far less destructive than any other angle.
segments.textZh: 而且因为它，你知道，撞击得很重，但击中了耳朵。我也听到有人喊，子弹，子弹。你知道，趴下，趴下。因为我，你知道，我相当利落、相当迅速地俯下身去了，在我俯下去之后，有子弹正从我的头顶飞过。所以我很庆幸自己俯下去了。更大的奇迹是，我当时正看向枪手所在的确切方向。所以它击中了。它以一个比其他任何角度破坏性都小得多的角度击中了我。

segments.textEn: So that was the miracle. That was for those people that don't believe in God. I think we got to all start thinking about that. You have to. You know, I'm a believer now. I'm more of a believer, I think. And a lot of people have said that to me. A lot of great people have said that to me, actually. But it was amazing that I happened to be turned just at that perfect angle and all because I put down a chart on immigration that showed that the numbers were so great.
segments.textZh: 所以那就是奇迹。对于那些不相信上帝的人来说，我认为我们都得开始思考这件事了。你必须这么做。你知道，我现在是个信徒了。我想，我更加相信了。而且很多人都对我这么说过。事实上，很多了不起的人都对我这么说过。但令人惊叹的是，我碰巧刚好转到了那个完美的角度，而这一切都是因为我放下了一张关于移民问题的图表，它显示那些数字非常出色。

segments.textEn: I love that chart even.
segments.textZh: 我甚至很喜欢那张图表。

segments.textEn: Maybe it's a sign. Maybe that's a sign.
segments.textZh: 也许这是个征兆。也许那是个征兆。

segments.textEn: It's an immigration sign.
segments.textZh: 这是一个移民标志。

segments.textEn: Well, the amazing thing is that the sign. I said, bring down that sign on immigration. And it was literally about an eighth of a second where it would be good. As, you know, we lost somebody. That was great. Corey, who a firefighter, a great gentleman, a great.
segments.textZh: 嗯，令人惊叹的是那块标牌。我说，把那块关于移民的标牌放下来。而从字面上说，只有大约1/8秒的时间会没事。再晚一点，无论你面朝哪个方向，都会是一场灾难。但它就是形成了那个完美的角度，正好对着这名枪手。非常悲惨的情况。如此悲惨的情况。正如，你知道，我们失去了一个人。那很了不起。科里，他是一名消防员，一位了不起的绅士，一位了不起的。

segments.textZh: 一位了不起的特朗普支持者。他是一个，简直是一个了不起的家庭和一个了不起的人。我的一个朋友走过来，埃隆，说，我想给这个家庭提供某种帮助。我说，那太好了。他说，你介意吗，我说，我完全不介意。然后他开出了一张100万美元的支票。给了。把它给了那位妻子。而且，你知道，她说，这真的很好，但我更希望我的丈夫回来。老实说，这话由一个人说出来很美好。

And we thought we. My first question was, because I heard bullets flying over me.
segments.textZh: 她。她很了不起。这个家庭很了不起。我们为他们以及另外2位先生筹集了很多钱，他们都是不可思议的人。他们也受了非常重的伤。人们以为他们撑不过去了，但他们撑过来了。我告诉你，巴特勒地区的医生们非常了不起。他们救了那2个人，而他们确实伤得很重，2个人伤势同样严重。而我们以为我们。我的第一个问题是，因为我听到子弹从我头顶飞过。

segments.textEn: I said, how many people were killed? Because we had a massive crowd there, a tremendous. Thousands and thousands of people, and there was no land. I mean, it was just. It was all people. So I said, how many people have been killed? Because I knew there were other shots being fired.
segments.textZh: 我说，有多少人遇害了？因为我们那里有一大群人，非常庞大。成千上万的人，而且没有空地。我是说，那简直。那里全是人。所以我说，有多少人遇害了？因为我知道还有其他枪声响起。

segments.textEn: Sure.
segments.textZh: 当然。

segments.textEn: And they said, we don't know yet, but some people have been badly hurt. And I have to give the Secret Service sniper, they call him or sharpshooter, but sniper, because he didn't know there was a problem. He's been. And he used one bullet from very far away, I guess probably about 400 yards.
segments.textZh: 他们说，我们还不知道，但有些人受了重伤。而且我必须给那名特勤局狙击手，他们这么称呼他，或者叫神枪手，但狙击手，因为他之前不知道出了问题。他一直。他显然是一位非凡的射手，而他不知道出了问题。他能够在5秒内把这一切都辨认出来。而且他从非常远的地方用了1颗子弹，我猜大概有400码。

segments.textEn: The shooter was 130, but he was on the. He was on the opposite side of the field and the podium, and he saw the. I mean, if he would have. A lot of people. A lot more people have been. Could have been badly hurt and killed. So I.
segments.textZh: 枪手距离是130，但他当时在。他当时在场地和讲台的另一侧，然后他看到了。枪口冒出的烟和火光，立刻辨认出来，并立即开了一枪。那是从非常远的地方射出的1次完美射击。而如果他。如果他没有那么做，埃隆，他本来会。我是说，如果他本来会。很多人。多得多的人已经。可能会受到重伤和死亡。所以我。

segments.textEn: I have to take my hat off to him because that's also a surreal. You know, he's been with them for 23 years, and he's never had anything like this. And all of a sudden he has to act, and it's a very tough thing to act and to be shooting somebody. But he saw the. He saw the gun, saw the smoke, saw the flame from the gun very far away. Obviously has very good eyes. He's got very good vision, which I assume you have to have in that particular work.
segments.textZh: 我必须向他致敬，因为那同样是一种超现实。你知道，他跟他们共事了23年，从来没遇到过这样的事。突然之间，他必须采取行动，而要采取行动、要向某个人开枪，是一件非常艰难的事。但他看到了。他看到了枪，看到了烟，看到了从很远处枪口冒出的火光。显然他的眼睛非常好。他的视力非常好，我想从事那项特殊工作，你必须具备这一点。

segments.textEn: But he. He took aim very quickly, and it was. They say it was approximately five seconds from long range, one bullet. If that didn't happen because the shooter had a lot of bullets. He had a lot of, a lot of cartridges up there with him. So what have been great.
segments.textZh: 但他。他非常迅速地瞄准了，而那是。他们说，从远距离算起大约是5秒，1颗子弹。如果那没有发生，因为枪手有很多子弹。他在那里随身带了很多、很多弹药。所以什么一直很棒。

segments.textEn: I mean, I mean that, that, that's clearly, you know, you know, he was, he was very competent in taking that shot to stop the, the assassin, the attempted assassination. But, but I mean, that does seem to be, I mean, some pretty significant failings elsewhere in the system. Like, there's just no way that, like how on earth does a shooter get on a roof 130 yards away? That seems crazy. I think most people, like people are wondering how that on earth could such a thing happen.
segments.textZh: 我是说，我是说，那、那、那显然，你知道，你知道，他、他开枪阻止那个、那个刺客、那次暗杀未遂时非常称职。但是、但是我的意思是，系统其他地方似乎确实存在一些相当严重的失误。比如，根本不可能，像是一个枪手究竟怎么会登上130码外的一处屋顶？这似乎太疯狂了。我想大多数人，像是人们都在想，这种事情究竟怎么可能发生。

segments.textEn: Well, you know, I view it as two ways. There should have been nobody on the roof. There were people because there were so many tens of thousands of people there. Probably, yeah, there's a guy with a gun.
segments.textZh: 嗯，你知道，我从2个方面看这件事。屋顶上本来不该有任何人。那里有很多人，因为现场有数以万计的人。有人看到了他。还有1个穿红色衬衫的女人，衣服上到处都是特朗普，她在尖叫，那家伙有枪。你知道，你看到了吗？大概看到了，是的，有个家伙拿着枪。

segments.textEn: I mean, it's like I'm just, I'm just, I guess, I mean, for my part, and I think probably many members of the public are wondering how the heck are, you know, basically people wondering why, pointing out there's a guy on the roof with a gun.
segments.textZh: 我是说，这就像我只是，我只是，我想，我是说，就我而言，而且我想可能很多公众都在想，到底怎么会，你知道，基本上人们都在想为什么，指出屋顶上有个拿枪的人。

segments.textEn: They're seeing it, but somehow it's not being addressed. That does seem crazy.
segments.textZh: 他们看到了，但不知怎么却没人处理。这确实显得很疯狂。

segments.textEn: Well, they're going to learn from this. The communication between the local police who sort of had an idea. He thought he was probably going to get shot, but you know, he was like pulling himself up and because of that he couldn't get to his gun and he fell down, actually very badly hurt his leg, his ankle, I hear very badly.
segments.textZh: 嗯，他们会从这件事中吸取教训。当地警方之间的沟通，他们算是有所察觉。然后最终有一个人把自己拉上屋顶，几乎做不到，因为他正把自己往上拉，而他看到了那个持枪的人。那个持枪的人用枪指着他。他觉得自己可能会中枪，但你知道，他当时正把自己往上拉，因此没法拿到自己的枪，于是摔了下去，腿部，脚踝，其实伤得很重，我听说伤得非常严重。

segments.textEn: But he fell down and he did, you know, from what I understand, he did say there's a guy up there with a gun. And the shooting started very quickly after that. I think it forced the shooter to go maybe quicker. You know, he was supposed to be a very good shot.
segments.textZh: 但他摔了下去，而且你知道，据我了解，他确实说了，上面有个人拿着枪。然后不久之后枪击就开始了。我认为这迫使枪手可能更快地行动。你知道，据说他枪法非常好。

segments.textEn: Yeah.
segments.textZh: 是的。

You know, you had so many people. One of the miracles was that nobody ran.
segments.textZh: 这不是远距离射击。特勤局那个人才是远距离射击，实际上，他的距离是，你知道，3 倍。所以，你知道，这是一件可怕的事。听着，这很难。我必须这样评价特勤局。当我倒下时，而且，你知道，我是基于……倒下的。我想他们在大喊，但其他人也在喊，因为人们看到了事情发生。你知道，当时有那么多人。其中一个奇迹是没有人逃跑。

segments.textEn: I mean, if a gun goes off, the crowd control people showed, showed us this. When guns go off, and it does happen in stadiums, at a soccer match or some kind of a match, everybody flees. They call it a stampede, like cattle, but everybody. And a lot of people get killed with those stampedes. We had more people than you'd have at, you know, some of these matches or these games, and nobody left. You know, you had a small group behind us in the grandstand, and that was full.
segments.textZh: 我是说，如果枪响了，人群管控人员向我们展示过这一点。枪响时，而这种情况确实会发生在体育场里，在足球比赛或某种比赛上，所有人都会逃跑。他们称之为踩踏，就像牛群一样，但所有人都会逃。很多人会在那些踩踏事件中丧生。我们的人数比你知道的某些比赛或这些赛事的人数还多，却没有人离开。你知道，我们身后的看台上有一小群人，那里坐满了。

segments.textEn: And you look at it as it was taking place. And normally they'd be running. They didn't leave. They saw that I was hurt. segments.textZh: 好吧，所以我们会去，你和我会去，我们会在委内瑞拉开个会、吃顿晚餐。委内瑞拉。因为现在发生的就是这种事。他们的犯罪率正在下降，而我们的犯罪率却直冲云霄。而且事情就是这么简单。你还什么都没见识到呢，因为这些人已经进入了我们的国家，他们才刚开始适应，而且他们不了解什么政治正确、执法或缺乏执法。

segments.textEn: And our police. I have to just end with this. We have great police, we have great law enforcement, but they're not allowed to do their job. They have to be able to do their job without being destroyed.
segments.textZh: 还有我们的警察。我必须用这个来结束。我们有很棒的警察，我们有很棒的执法人员，但他们不被允许履行职责。他们必须能够履行职责，而不被毁掉。

segments.textEn: Well, absolutely. And it's obviously demoralizing if you're a police officer risking your life to, you know, to, you know, to arrest violent criminals who could kill you and do kill you sometimes, and then you arrest the violent criminal and then the, the D.A. you know, doesn't prosecute and end up let the guy out. Well then, like, why, why should a police officer risk their life to arrest a violent felon?
segments.textZh: 嗯，完全正确。而且，如果你是一名警察，冒着生命危险去，你知道，去，你知道，去逮捕那些可能杀死你、而且有时确实会杀死你的暴力罪犯，这显然会让人士气低落；然后你逮捕了暴力罪犯，接着，那个，那个地方检察官，你知道，却不起诉，最后把那家伙放了。那这样的话，一名警察为什么，为什么应该冒着生命危险去逮捕一名暴力重罪犯呢？

segments.textEn: Well, even worse, nothing's going to happen. Even worse, they prosecute the police officer. They, they go after and they prosecute the police officer and they take away his pension, they take away his job, he loses his family, he loses his house.
segments.textZh: 嗯，更糟的是，什么事都不会发生。更糟的是，他们起诉警察。他们，他们追究并起诉警察，还夺走他的养老金，夺走他的工作，他失去家庭，失去房子。

segments.textEn: Well, I thought it was very telling, like incredibly telling that, you know, when that, there was that case where, you know, sort of a gang of thugs beat up police officers, I think it was in Times Square in New York. I mean that, that is, that is a, that is a gross indignity against the United States.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我觉得这非常能说明问题，简直太能说明问题了，你知道，当时有那么一个案件，你知道，好像是一伙暴徒殴打警察，我想是在纽约时代广场。而，而，而后来那些家伙什么事都没有。他们，他们以零保释金获释了。而且我想，他们当中有一群人还拿到了去加利福尼亚的免费票。嗯，为什么会。我是说，这，这，这是对美国的严重羞辱。

segments.textEn: And, and that's how, I mean, this is insane. Like, have we lost all pride? What that, how can such a thing be allowed to occur?
segments.textZh: 而，而事情就是这样，我是说，这太疯狂了。就像，我们已经完全失去自尊了吗？那，怎么能允许这种事情发生？

segments.textEn: I've never seen anything, you know, we see where they get shot is very dangerous profession, but something they're very proud of and they want to be able to do their job. But I've seen them get shot. I've seen a lot of things, but I've never seen where these guys are standing in the middle of a big street, everybody watching them, and they're literally boxing, like punching, stand up, fighting a police officer. There were two of them and you had about six of these guys and they're punching the hell out of them.
segments.textZh: 我从没见过这样的事，你知道，我们看到他们中枪，这是一种非常危险的职业，但也是他们非常自豪的事情，而且他们希望能够履行自己的职责。但我见过他们中枪。我见过很多事情，但我从没见过这些家伙站在一条大街中央，所有人都看着他们，而他们真的像在打拳一样，挥拳，站着，和一名警察打架。有2名警察，而这些家伙大约有6个，他们把警察往死里打。

segments.textEn: And in their own country, they would be dead if they did that. They'd be shot. Yeah, they would be shot instantly. And you know, they come from these countries and it's taking them a while to realize that we don't do that in this country. But in their own country, if they stood on a street and had a fight with a police officer, they would be shot. There's no political correctness. And it's such a sad, it's such a sad thing to see.
segments.textZh: 而在他们自己的国家，如果他们这么做，他们早就死了。他们会被枪杀。是的，他们会立刻被枪杀。而且你知道，他们来自这些国家，他们需要一段时间才能意识到，我们在这个国家不会那么做。但在他们自己的国家，如果他们站在街上和一名警察打架，他们会被枪杀。那里没有政治正确。而看到这种事太令人难过了，太令人难过了。

segments.textEn: And that's the reason you have crime, by the way, because we don't do anything about it.
segments.textZh: 顺便说一句，这就是你会有犯罪问题的原因，因为我们对此什么都不做。

segments.textEn: Yeah, we just cannot have a situation where our police officers be beaten up on camera by, you know, a gang of illegal immigrants and then nothing happens to the guys that beat up the cops. I mean, and they're let out. This is unacceptable.
segments.textZh: 是的，我们绝不能出现这样的局面：我们的警察被，你知道，一伙非法移民当着镜头殴打，之后那些殴打警察的家伙却什么事都没有。我是说，而且他们还被放了。这是不可接受的。

segments.textEn: We're going to change it and we're going to get them out of the country. You know, when I first got involved, they said you couldn't get them back to these countries, you couldn't take them back. In the case of Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, some others, you couldn't get them back. And I said, really? Oh, you can't get it back? Because under Obama, he couldn't get them back. They'd put up, they'd fly them in and they'd put planes on the runways in these countries so you couldn't land a plane.
segments.textZh: 我们要改变这种情况，我们要把他们赶出这个国家。你知道，我刚开始参与的时候，他们说你无法把他们送回这些国家，你无法把他们带回去。就危地马拉、洪都拉斯、萨尔瓦多和其他一些国家而言，你无法把他们送回去。我说，真的吗？哦，你不能把他们送回去？因为在奥巴马执政期间，他无法把他们送回去。他们会……他们会把他们空运过去，而那些国家会把飞机停在跑道上，让你的飞机无法降落。

segments.textEn: They'd bring them back. And the general told me, the generals told me, sir, we can't bring them back to countries. Won't accept Ms. 13 gang members, they won't accept them. And I said, really? How much do we pay these various countries in terms of economic aid? Which is also somewhat ridiculous. And the answer was $750 million. I said, good. Tell them they're in default, they're delinquent, we're not going to do, we're not paying them anymore because they won't accept it.
segments.textZh: 他们会把他们送回去。那位将军告诉我，那些将军告诉我，先生，我们无法把他们送回那些国家。它们不接收 MS-13 帮派成员，它们不接收他们。我说，真的吗？我们以经济援助的形式向这些不同国家支付多少钱？这本身也有些荒谬。而答案是7.5亿美元。我说，很好。告诉他们，他们违约了，他们拖欠了，我们不会再这么做，我们不会再给他们钱，因为他们不接受。

segments.textEn: And you know what happened? They all called me, every one of them. They said, we would be honored to take them back, sir. We would be honored. It was so easy. But it's one of those things. And we got them back. We took in so many. You know, Ms. 13 is probably the worst gangs in the world. They're the most vicious, violent. We took them out of here by the thousands and got them out of here and their countries took them back.
segments.textZh: 你知道后来发生了什么吗？他们全都给我打了电话，一个不落。他们说，先生，我们很荣幸把他们接回去。我们很荣幸。事情就是这么容易。但这就是那类事情之一。而且我们把他们送回去了。我们接收了太多。你知道，MS-13 可能是世界上最恶劣的帮派。他们最为凶残、暴力。我们把他们成千上万地从这里带走，让他们离开这里，而他们的国家把他们接了回去。

segments.textEn: And because I said, you're not getting any more economic aid. And once they said that they were nice, they wouldn't take them back for Obama. They wouldn't take them back for anybody. And now we have a problem because we have this guy and they, again, they don't take them back anymore with Biden because they don't respect him.
segments.textZh: 而这是因为我说，你们不会再得到任何经济援助。一旦他们那么说，他们就很好说话了，他们不愿意为奥巴马把他们接回去。他们不愿意为任何人把他们接回去。而现在我们遇到了问题，因为我们有这个家伙，而且他们，同样，在拜登执政期间，他们不再把他们接回去，因为他们不尊重他。

segments.textEn: Yeah, yeah. So it's just gotta, it's gotta be done. We, we just can't, can't have.
segments.textZh: 是的，是的。所以这事就是必须，必须完成。我们，我们就是不能，不能有。

segments.textEn: Whether they're citizens or not, citizens we can't have because they won't prosecute citizens either. Not just legals. So you can't have violent, repeat violent offenders that are not, that don't get incarcerated because they will obviously, by definition continue to, to hurt people. And I think where part of this comes from is that there's, I do sort of consider myself liberal in some ways. I mean, it's just that you want to have empathy for people.
segments.textZh: 无论他们是不是公民，公民也不能这样，因为他们也不会起诉公民。不只是合法移民。所以你不能让那些暴力的、屡次实施暴力的犯罪者不被，不被监禁，因为显然，按照定义，他们会继续，继续伤害别人。我认为，其中一部分原因在于，有，我在某些方面确实算是自由派。我是说，只是因为你希望对人们抱有同理心。

segments.textEn: Obviously you want to have empathy for people. I totally agree with that. You want to have empathy, but you also have to have empathy for the victims of the criminals. And if you just have empathy for the criminals, it's actually shallow empathy. It's not real. You're not thinking, you're not. You have one layer, deep empathy. You got to say, like, if you don't incarcerate this person, who are they going to hurt? They might kill someone, they might rape someone.
segments.textZh: 显然，你希望对人们抱有同理心。我完全赞同这一点。你希望有同理心，但你也必须对罪犯的受害者抱有同理心。而如果你只对罪犯抱有同理心，那其实是浅层的同理心。不是真正的同理心。你没有在思考，你没有。你的同理心只有一层深。你必须这样想，比如，如果你不监禁这个人，他们会伤害谁？他们可能会杀人，他们可能会强奸别人。

segments.textEn: If you don't incarcerate them, you have to have empathy for the victims. And there's a lack of empathy for the victims of the criminals, and too much empathy for the criminals. It doesn't make sense. That's why you want to have deep empathy for society as a whole, not shallow empathy for criminals.
segments.textZh: 如果你不监禁他们，你必须对受害者抱有同理心。现在缺乏对罪犯受害者的同理心，却对罪犯有太多同理心。这说不通。这就是为什么你要对整个社会抱有深层的同理心，而不是对罪犯抱有浅层的同理心。

segments.textEn: And we have to give our police officers the dignity and the respect that they deserve. And we have to let them do their job. They can do a great job, but we have to let them do their job. And if we don't do that, you know, it's going to all disappear. There's never been a society like this where you're allowed to do anything you want and nothing happens. And I'm talking about violent crime. And it's going to get more violent because these are really, really violent people.
segments.textZh: 而且我们必须给予我们的警察他们应得的尊严和尊重。我们必须让他们履行职责。他们可以把工作做得很好，但我们必须让他们履行职责。如果我们不这么做，你知道，一切都会消失。从来没有哪个社会像这样，允许你为所欲为，却什么后果都没有。我说的是暴力犯罪。而且它会变得更加暴力，因为这些人真的、真的非常暴力。

segments.textEn: And we're going to get them out of our country and we're going to get them back to where, because they were sent here by the presidents and by the various people that run those countries. And I know every one of those guys, and they're smart people and they're streetwise people and they really think that the USA is stupid. They think we're run by stupid people and they happen to be right. But when I was there, we had no problem.
segments.textZh: 而我们要把他们赶出我们的国家，我们要把他们送回原来的地方，因为是那些总统和管理那些国家的各类人士把他们送到这里来的。我认识那些家伙中的每一个，他们都很聪明，都很懂街头那一套，而且他们真的认为美国很愚蠢。他们认为我们由一群蠢人管理，而他们碰巧是对的。但我在任的时候，我们没有问题。

segments.textEn: We got them out. We took out thousands of Ms. 13 gang members, we brought them back and now again, they, it's the same old story. We don't do it. And they actually gave them a big increase in aid. They raised it up to billions of dollars and they get nothing for it. So, you know, it's, it's. I hope everybody's going to vote for Trump and we're going to get this country straight. And I didn't need this. I'm like, I didn't need this.
segments.textZh: 我们把他们赶出去了。我们清除了数千名 Ms. 13 帮派成员，把他们送了回去，而现在又来了，他们，还是老一套。我们不这么做。而且他们实际上还大幅增加了对他们的援助。他们把金额提高到了数十亿美元，却什么也没换来。所以，你知道，这，这。我希望每个人都会投票给特朗普，我们会让这个国家重回正轨。而我本不需要这些。我就像，我本不需要这些。

segments.textEn: I had a very nice life. I didn't need to go through court systems and go through all the other stuff and run at the same time. I have to run. I have to go through fake trials with, in some cases, corrupt judges, totally corrupt judges. I didn't need it. I had a nice life. I have great locations. I have beautiful oceans that I have places. You know, this was. But I felt it was important and if I had to do it over again, you probably think I'm crazy for doing it, actually.
segments.textZh: 我原本过着非常美好的生活。我本不需要经历法院系统和经历所有其他那些事，同时还要竞选。我必须竞选。我必须经历虚假的审判，有些案件中，是腐败的法官，彻底腐败的法官。我本不需要这些。我原本生活得很好。我有很棒的地点。我有美丽的海洋，我在那里有地方。你知道，这本来是。但我觉得这很重要，如果让我再来一次，你大概会觉得我这么做很疯狂，真的。

segments.textEn: But if I had to do it over again, I would have done it over again because this is so much more important than me or my life. This is. We're going to save this country. This country is going down. And these people are bad people that we're running against. And they're liars. They make statements. They do things that are so bad. They say they're going to make a strong border. They say they've been great on the border and they've been the worst in history.
segments.textZh: 但如果让我再来一次，我还是会再做一次，因为这远比我或我的生活重要得多。这是。我们要拯救这个国家。这个国家正在走下坡路。而我们正在与之竞选的这些人都是坏人。而且他们是骗子。他们发表言论。他们做的事情非常糟糕。他们说他们要打造坚固的边境。他们说自己在边境问题上一直做得很出色，而他们却是历史上最糟糕的。

segments.textEn: They say they're going to stop crime.
segments.textZh: 他们说他们要制止犯罪。

segments.textEn: The facts speak for themselves.
segments.textZh: 事实不言自明。

segments.textEn: It's so incredible.
segments.textZh: 这太不可思议了。

segments.textEn: The facts speak for themselves. It's got to the point where people just don't even bother reporting crime in a lot of states because they know nothing that's going to happen. You know, that's what I hear anecdotally from people all the time. So, you know, it's just, you know, my values, I'm just saying to people out there, like, my, you know, the things I think are important for the future is like we've got to have safe cities, we're going to have secure borders, we've got to have sensible spending, and we've got to have deregulation.
segments.textZh: 事实不言自明。事情已经发展到这种地步，在许多州，人们甚至都懒得报案了，因为他们知道什么也不会发生。你知道，这就是我一直从人们那里听到的种种说法。所以，你知道，就是，你知道，我的价值观，我只是想对外面的人说，比如，我的，你知道，我认为对未来很重要的事情是，我们必须有安全的城市，我们要有安全的边境，我们必须进行合理的支出，而且我们必须放松监管。

segments.textEn: And so we can have a prosperous future. And then we want to have some exciting, you know, sort of moonshot projects that people can get fired up about. And, you know, that's. That's the future I'm looking for. And, you know, I'm pro environment, but I'm not against, you know, I'm not like, I don't think we should vilify the oil and gas industry because they're keeping civilization going right now. And. But I do think we want to move, you know, you know, a reasonable speed towards a sustainable energy economy.
segments.textZh: 这样我们才能拥有繁荣的未来。然后，我们希望有一些令人振奋的，你知道，某种登月式项目，让人们能为之振奋。而且，你知道，那就是。那就是我所期待的未来。而且，你知道，我支持环保，但我并不反对，你知道，我不是那种，我不认为我们应该妖魔化石油和天然气行业，因为它们现在正维系着文明的运转。而且。但我确实认为，我们希望以，你知道，你知道，合理的速度迈向可持续能源经济。

segments.textEn: Those are my values. And I think, you know, and so, I mean, that's why I'm supporting you for president, you know.
segments.textZh: 这些就是我的价值观。而且我认为，你知道，所以，我的意思是，这就是我支持你竞选总统的原因，你知道。

segments.textEn: Well, I appreciate it. We're going to make. We're going to give incentive to companies to come into our country, not to leave our country. We're going to be giving tremendous incentives. We want companies to build here, not to build in other locations. And we want to create jobs. And again, it's about the American dream. You don't hear about the American dream anymore, Elon. You don't hear you're the American dream in the truest sense, but you don't hear about the American dream anymore.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我很感激。我们要做到。我们将激励企业进入我们的国家，而不是离开我们的国家。我们将给予巨大的激励。我们希望企业在这里建设，而不是在其他地方建设。我们希望创造就业机会。再说一次，这关乎美国梦。现在已经听不到人们谈论美国梦了，埃隆。你就是最真正意义上的美国梦，但现在已经听不到人们谈论美国梦了。

segments.textEn: And you're going to hear about it. People, they need that incentive to Go out and do it. And they're going to love their lives. I mean, they're going to love. They're going to look forward to getting up in the morning and going to, you know, going to a job that they love. Not a job that they can't stand or not any job at all where they have no money, where they literally have no money. And then they end up with violence and lots of other problems to no, we're going to do.
segments.textZh: 而你们将会听到。人们，他们需要那种激励，走出去行动起来。他们将会热爱自己的生活。我的意思是，他们将会热爱。他们会期待早晨起床，去，你知道，去做一份他们热爱的工作。不是一份他们无法忍受的工作，也不是根本没有工作、没有钱，他们真的一分钱都没有。然后他们最终陷入暴力和许多其他问题，不，我们会做。

segments.textEn: We're going to do some great things. And I learned a lot in the first. We had a great economy and all of that. We rebuilt the military. We did so much. But I also learned. And I also learned the best people. I learned the good people, the smart people, the dumb people, the people that can do things. You know, you learn. When I first came in, I tell people I was in Washington, D.C. only 17 times. According to the fake news media, I was in 17 times.
segments.textZh: 我们会做一些了不起的事情。我在第一次时学到了很多。我们拥有很棒的经济以及这一切。我们重建了军队。我们做了很多。但我也学到了。而且我也了解了最优秀的人。我了解了好人、聪明人、愚蠢的人、能做成事情的人。你知道，你会学到东西。我刚上任时，我告诉人们，我只去过华盛顿特区17次。据假新闻媒体说，我去过17次。

segments.textEn: I never stayed over. And you don't know people. You rely on other people to give you names, and then you realize the people you relied on weren't so good. Now, we had great people, but we also had some where I wouldn't have, you know, used them had I known. Now I know everybody, and I think we're going to. We're going to really turn things around fast. We have no choice otherwise, we're not going to have a country. And I really appreciate this has been.
segments.textZh: 我从未在那里过夜。而且你不了解那些人。你依靠其他人给你提供名字，然后你意识到，你所依靠的那些人并没有那么好。我们当时有很棒的人，但也有一些人，如果我早知道，我就不会，你知道，用他们。现在我认识所有人，我认为我们将会。我们真的会迅速扭转局面。我们别无选择，否则我们将不再拥有一个国家。我真的很感激，这一直是。

segments.textEn: To me, it's been a lot of fun being with you. You're an amazing guy. You've done an incredible job and a great inspiration to people, a great inspiration. And I hope you keep going and just continue to do well. And we're going to have a big election coming up, And I think November 5th will be the most important day in the history of our country. I think that election will be the most important election, and I think it'll end up being maybe the most important day in the history of our country.
segments.textZh: 对我来说，和你在一起非常有趣。你是个了不起的人。你做得令人难以置信，是人们的巨大鼓舞，巨大的鼓舞。我希望你继续前进，继续做得很好。我们即将迎来一场重大选举，我认为11月5日将是我国历史上最重要的一天。我认为那场选举将是最重要的选举，而且我认为它最终可能会成为我国历史上最重要的一天。

segments.textEn: Because if we don't win, I just feel so sorry for everybody.
segments.textZh: 因为如果我们赢不了，我只是觉得所有人都太可怜了。

segments.textEn: No, I think we're at a fork in the road of destiny, of civilization, and I think we need to take the right path. And I think you're the right path. So I think that's what it comes down to.
segments.textZh: 不，我认为我们正处在命运与文明的道路岔口，我认为我们需要选择正确的道路。而且我认为你就是正确的道路。所以我认为归根结底就是这样。

segments.textEn: Thank you very much, Elon. It's a great honor, and we'll do it again sometime. And it's been really fun. And I hope you got a lot of viewers. I hear you got a lot, but I hope you got a lot. I know you got a lot of them. So I appreciate it. I'll see you soon.
segments.textZh: 非常感谢你，埃隆。这是莫大的荣幸，我们以后找时间再来一次。真的非常有趣。我希望你吸引了很多观众。我听说有很多，但我希望你吸引了很多。我知道你吸引了很多观众。所以我很感激。回头见。

segments.textEn: All right, Sounds good. Thank you.
segments.textZh: 好的，听起来不错。谢谢。

segments.textEn: Thank you, Elon. Thank you very much. Bye.
segments.textZh: 谢谢你，埃隆。非常感谢。再见。
